subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Bone sarcomas: osteosarcoma, Ewing sarcoma and chondrosarcoma management

steps.tx: Primary bone malignancy displays distinctive anatomical predispositions and biological behaviors. **Osteosarcoma** typically arises in the metaphysis of adolescent long bones, defined histologically by malignant mesenchymal spindle cells producing immature osteoid matrix. Classical radiological hallmarks include periosteal elevation forming **Codman triangle**, aggressive cortical breakthrough, and extensive cloud-like osteoblastic mineralisation with sunburst periosteal reaction extending into adjacent soft tissues.
steps.say: Primary bone malignancy displays distinctive anatomical predispositions and biological behaviors. left.title: Osteosarcoma Features
points: Malignant osteoid production is diagnostic sine qua non
Codman triangle and sunburst periosteal reaction

right.title: Ewing Sarcoma Features
points: Peak incidence in children and young teens (5-15 yrs)
Diaphyseal or metadiaphyseal flat and long bones
Small round blue cell histology without matrix

steps.tx: Curative management of localized high-grade osteosarcoma requires systemic chemotherapy paired with limb-sparing resection. Standard multi-agent chemotherapy follows the **MAP regimen**, comprising high-dose methotrexate with leucovorin rescue, doxorubicin, and **cisplatin**. Administered in neoadjuvant and adjuvant phases, histological tumour necrosis of 90% or greater in the resected surgical specimen defines good pathological response, predicting superior long-term event-free survival.

steps.tx: Specific chromosomal translocations drive pathogenesis in primitive neuroectodermal bone tumours. **Ewing sarcoma** is characterized by reciprocal chromosomal translocation **t(11;22)(q24;q12)** in approximately 85% to 90% of cases, generating the pathogenic EWSR1-FLI1 aberrant fusion transcription factor. Histologically appearing as uniform small round blue cells, immunohistochemistry reveals intense membranous CD99 MIC2 positivity, while periodic acid-Schiff staining demonstrates abundant cytoplasmic glycogen.

Ewing sarcoma is characterized by reciprocal chromosomal translocation t(11;22)(q24;q12) in approximately 85% to 90% of cases, generating the pathogenic EWSR1-FLI1 fusion transcription factor. Cells display intense membranous CD99 positivity and abundant cytoplasmic glycogen.

rows: Definitive molecular confirmation via FISH or RT-PCR
Seen in ~10% of atypical fusion cases

steps.tx: Intensive multi-agent systemic chemotherapy forms the foundation of Ewing sarcoma curative regimens. Standard systemic therapy utilizes alternating cycles of **VDC/IE chemotherapy**, alternating vincristine, doxorubicin, and cyclophosphamide with ifosfamide and etoposide. In the randomized Euro-EWING 99 and AEWS0031 trials, shortening the inter-cycle interval from 3 weeks to a 2-week **interval-compressed schedule** with G-CSF support significantly improved event-free and overall survival in localized disease.

steps.tx: Cartilage-forming neoplasms display unique radiobiological resistance and insensitivity to systemic cytotoxics. Conventional **chondrosarcoma** is intrinsically chemoresistant and radioresistant, attributed to abundant avascular extracellular chondroid matrix, slow cellular proliferation, and overexpression of multidrug-resistance transport pumps. Consequently, wide **surgical resection** with negative surgical margins R0 remains the only curative therapeutic modality for non-metastatic conventional and dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma.
steps.say: Cartilage-forming neoplasms display unique radiobiological resistance and insensitivity to systemic cytotoxics. Conventional chondrosarcoma is intrinsically chemoresistant and radioresistant, attributed to abundant avascular extracellular matrix, slow proliferation, and overexpression of multidrug-resistance pumps. Wide surgical resection with clear margins remains the only curative modality.

left.title: Conventional Chondrosarcoma
points: Cure achieved solely via R0 surgical resection

right.title: Mesenchymal / Dedifferentiated
points: High propensity for early haematogenous metastases

steps.tx: Molecular profiling in conventional chondrosarcomas reveals actionable metabolic mutations. Somatic gain-of-function point mutations in **IDH1 or IDH2** occur in up to 50% of central chondrosarcomas and are pathognomonic of Ollier disease and Maffucci syndrome. Mutant isocitrate dehydrogenase produces the oncometabolite **2-hydroxyglutarate** 2-HG, which competitively inhibits alpha-ketoglutarate-dependent histone and DNA demethylases, inducing hypermethylation and cellular dedifferentiation.

steps.tx: Isolated pulmonary recurrence represents a unique potentially curable oligometastatic state. In relapsed osteosarcoma without extrapulmonary disease, aggressive complete surgical resection via **pulmonary metastasectomy** achieves long-term post-relapse survival exceeding 30% to 40%. Repeated surgical thoracotomies or stereotactic ablative radiotherapy are indicated provided all anatomical metastatic deposits are resectable with adequate post-resection pulmonary functional reserve.

left.title: Favourable Metastasectomy Candidates
points: Unilateral or limited bilateral lung nodules

right.title: Poor Prognostic Factors in Relapse
points: Early relapse during primary MAP chemotherapy
Multiple bilateral pleural or diaphragmatic deposits

steps.tx: Osteoclast-mediated bone osteolysis drives structural bone destruction in giant cell tumours. **Denosumab** is a fully human IgG2 monoclonal antibody that binds **RANKL**, neutralizing osteoclast activation. In unresectable or locally advanced giant cell tumour of bone, denosumab eliminates reactive multinucleated osteoclast-like giant cells, promotes dense fibro-osseous stromal reconstitution, and remineralises cortical boundaries, enabling joint preservation or definitive surgical resection.

rows: Ablation of osteoclast giant cells, re-ossification
Sacral / pelvic giant cell tumour downstaging
Anti-angiogenic tumour necrosis in refractory relapse
